🤔 Turkey moves to bring Kurds into its orbit as US influence wanes
Turkey is pressing ahead with a strategic opening toward its Kurdish population, betting that a peace deal could extend the country's influence well beyond its borders, The Cradle reports.
The window of opportunity opened after the US reliance on the "Kurdish card," a strategic tool it has used since the Cold War, failed against Iran.
🔴 US was unable to mobilize either the Kurds of Iran or the larger Kurdish groups in Iraq, despite decades of investment in those relationships.
🔴 In Syria, the US-backed Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) have collapsed, with their geopolitical project of building an autonomous Kurdish region now largely dismantled as the US steps aside
This has created a strategic opening for Turkey. It has eliminated the military and territorial threat posed by armed Kurdish groups in Syria, advancing its goal of subordinating the region and expanding its influence eastward.
The Kurdish opening is part of a broader Turkish strategy to establish itself as the dominant power in West Asia:
🔴 Turkey has signed a joint defense agreement with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, signaling its ambition to lead an emerging Sunni-majority bloc
🔴 Turkey is seeking to expand its influence from the Caspian Sea to the Mediterranean, positioning itself as a central player in the region's new security architecture
🔴 It is deepening economic and military ties across the region, including drone sales, military academies, and scholarships that build lasting influence
At home, President Erdogan has a huge stake in making sure the peace plan succeeds. He aims to dissolve the decade-old opposition bloc led by the pro-Kurdish DEM Party and the Republican People's Party, which stand in the way of prolonging his already protracted tenure. Erdogan has been courting the DEM Party to help change the constitution and secure additional terms in exchange for enhanced recognition of Kurdish rights.
👉 However, opposition voices warn that Erdogan's gestures of peace toward Kurds are little more than a political ploy to gain popularity and extend his term in office.
For decades, the Kurdish conflict has been a domestic headache for Turkey. Now, Turkish leaders see an opportunity to turn the Kurdish issue into an instrument of regional influence. If Turkey can pacify its own Kurdish population, it will also position itself as the dominant power over Kurdish groups in Syria and Iraq, locking in Turkish influence across the region.

events.text:
🤥🤡 Trump’s ‘economic D-Day’ sanctions against Iran just hit a Chinese wall
🔊 “China has already stated many times that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions…China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests,” Foreign Ministry spox Lin Jian said at a briefing Tuesday, warning Washington not to “interfere with or disrupt” China’s trade with Iran.
His comments followed Trump Treasury chief Bessent’s threats to slap secondary sanctions on countries that continue to do business with Iran under a plan he’s dubbed “Operation Economic Outcast.” The measures include secondary restrictions across a broad array of sectors, from digital assets to shipping, aviation and gold, and threats to cut Iran’s trade partners off from the dollar system.
🔊 “No one is above this,” Bessent said after being asked specifically whether the new restrictions would affect China – Iran’s biggest trade partner. “This is economic asphyxiation of this regime…and no one should test our resolve.”
 
🤔 China’s options in dealing with Trump’s latest huffing and puffing? Endless.
 
They include:
🔴 use of small ‘teapot refineries’ operating only in China, insulating major state energy companies from the US restrictions. These refineries use yuan to avoid dollar clearing systems, and local Chinese banks with limited exposure to US correspondent accounts
🔴 use of alternative payment networks, including China’s Cross-Border Interbank Payment System
🔴 origin masking, including mid-ocean ship-to-ship transfers and relabeling of Iranian oil as Malaysian or Indonesian crude, giving importers a legal shield of plausible deniability, and complicating sanctions enforcers’ efforts to find a paper trail
🔴 using complex intermediaries, including long, hard-to-track chains of tiny shipping firms and brokers, some of them focused exclusively on Iranian oil purchases, making them effectively invulnerable to US threats
🔴 taking advantage of the Treasury’s traditional hesitation in imposing secondary sanctions out of fear of a trade escalation, or new Chinese restrictions on [rare earths and metals exports](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73579)
🔴 using strategic barter and investment accords with Iran, allowing financing to be bypassed entirely – with China getting discounted Iranian oil in exchange for manufacturing equipment, consumer goods, rail or port development, or any number of other options
🔴 deployment of “blocking statutes” – a Chinese Ministry of Commerce tool explicitly forbidding Chinese companies from complying with unilateral US sanctions
🔴 use of state-backed alternative insurance to keep tankers compliant with domestic port entry requirements, and outside Western maritime registries and regulations
🔴 activation of massive onshore “bonded” storage capacity, allowing Iranian oil to sit indefinitely without being recorded as passing through customs
If push comes to shove, China can just tell the US to buzz off. Otherwise, Beijing can just push the entire US manufacturing base and retail sector off a cliff.

🔊 “The Saudi-Israeli-American enemy and their mercenaries must realize that their old equations are now threadbare and no longer effective. Yemen, once surrounded by enemies, has now turned into a major power,” the commanders of Yemen’s Armed Forces said in joint statement.
🗣 “The slightest folly by enemies or their mercenaries will be met with a firestorm that will bring nothing but regret for adversaries,” the message warned. 
🔊 “Our forces are closely monitoring all enemy movements, and our fingers are on the trigger. Yemen will no longer serve as a battlefield, but be a graveyard for all conspirators and a hell for all aggressors.”
🗣 “The balance of power has completely changed. Yemen, thanks to reliance on homegrown capabilities and expertise, has acquired such destructive weapons that will force aggressors to pay a heavy price. There is no room for retreat or compromise. The future belongs to a free and independent Yemen.”
 
Houthis: a global force to be reckoned with?
 
🔴 Emerging from international obscurity when they seized power in a popular revolution in late 2014, the tribal warriors and guerrilla warfare experts proved their mettle against a conventionally, technologically and militarily superior adversary in the form of a 10-member Saudi-led coalition in 2015, surviving years of aerial bombardments, mercenary offensives, and a grueling naval blockade which caused a famine that killed over a hundred thousand people.
🔴 The genocidal aggression failed to break the Houthis, with the Gulf coalition forced to sign a ceasefire in April 2022.
🔴 In late 2023, the Houthis joined Hezbollah and Shia militias in Iraq as the only Arab forces to come to Gaza’s aid, targeting Israeli shipping and lobbing missiles and drones at Israeli cities. Their new asymmetric warfare capabilities, achieved with Iran’s help, became an unwelcome surprise for Tel Aviv.
🔴 Two US administrations tried to stop the Houthis – in 2024 and 2025, respectively – amassing massive armadas in and around the Red Sea, targeting the fighters in ground attacks and getting into pitched aerial and naval battles with their missiles and drones. The US ended up losing nearly two dozen Reaper drones and 3 Super Hornet jets, accidentally crashed a carrier into a civilian ship off Egypt, and had multiple other close calls. The Houthis’ grip on the strategic global maritime chokepoint? [Untouched.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65279)
🔴 In July, after a Saudi attack targeted a Houthi delegation returning from Iran at Sanaa’s airport, the Houthis imposed a blockade on the Kingdom’s Red Sea oil exports, and began strikes its oil production facilities, demonstrating their ability to control the strategic body of water without a blue water navy, and to evade the Gulf nation’s [NATO-delivered air defenses.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73556)
So yeah, the Houthis aren’t bluffing. They are a major regional power that even superpowers have to reckon with.

🔥 Iran doesn’t have to shoot down US Army’s attack helicopters: they’re doing just fine crashing on their own
The Army’s fearsome Apache helicopters, introduced in the mid-80s at the twilight at the Cold War to take on enemy armored columns, never got their chance to fly into Iranian territory to launch strikes during the Epstein coalition’s war.
👉 Instead, they’ve been crashing at near-historic highs, with five major crashes reported since October alone.
The gunships are suspected to be suffering from widespread mechanical problems, including transmission issues with the gunship’s newer, trouble-prone E-model – affecting everything from electrical power to hydraulics and tail rotor function.
📌 One incident proved deadly. On August 12, two airmen were killed during a routine maintenance training flight outside Fort Hood, Texas. The crash triggered a 100-acre wildfire.
The Army seems to have been aware of the problem, sending out an urgent safety message in April ordering a halt to flights amid reports of 70 transmissions with problems. A follow-up notice in July added ten units to the no-fly list, equivalent to ~1/10 or more of the Army’s entire attack chopper fleet.
🤔 Iran’s new strategy on handling the US attack chopper threat? Literally ‘do nothing, win.’
